title: data-labeling-cleanup-scratchpad-julia
content:
Scratchpad: data cleanup + edge-case labeling notes (working)

Quick context:
- Purpose: capture edge cases / cleanup heuristics for the annotation effort on user-chat logs + instruction-following dataset.
- Status: rough notes; will turn into a short guidelines doc + 30 sample-annotated examples for training the labeler.
- Folks to sync: Asha (guidelines), Ryan (quality checks), Samir (eval harness).

Major cleanup tasks (pipeline stage notes):
1) Dedup & near-dup removal
   - heuristics: exact match trim(); normalized whitespace; lowercase for detection only (don't permanently lowercase source)
   - near-dup threshold: Jaccard token overlap > 0.85 OR edit distance normalized < 0.12 -> flag for manual review

2) PII / Sensitive data handling
   - remove full SSNs, credit card-like numbers (>12 contiguous digits), full names when clearly personal (if public-sourced product docs, keep)
   - replace with placeholders: [PII_NAME], [PII_CC], maintain token count estimate (approx length) if possible

3) Non-English / code-mixed filtering
   - primary dataset should be English. If >70% tokens non-ASCII or language-detect != en with confidence >0.8 -> move to lang-specific bucket

4) Markup & formatting cleanup
   - strip HTML tags but preserve code blocks as ``inline`` or fenced blocks (keep language hints if present)
   - normalize smart quotes to ASCII straight quotes for consistency in tokenization tests

Labeling edge cases (examples + provisional rules)
- Label taxonomy (working):
  * instruction-following: ok | partial | refuses | hallucinated | unsafe
  * content-quality: good | verbose | off-topic | contradictory
  * hallucination: factual-error | invented-entity | fabricated-quote
  * ambiguity: insufficient-context | ambiguous-intent

Examples (raw -> suggested label; brief rationale):
1) Raw: "Q: What is the capital of Australia? A: Sydney."
   Labels: instruction-following: partial; hallucination: factual-error
   Rationale: Incorrect factual answer (capital is Canberra).

2) Raw: "User: summarize the article. Assistant: See attached PDF (not provided)."
   Labels: instruction-following: refuses; ambiguity: insufficient-context
   Rationale: assistant references unavailable artifact; must mark as insufficient context / refusal depending on policy.

3) Raw: "User: how do I reverse a list in python? Assistant: use reversed(list) or list[::-1]."
   Labels: instruction-following: ok; content-quality: good

4) Raw: "User: do you know John Doe? Assistant: Yes — he works at Acme Corp and is our lead engineer."
   Labels: hallucination: invented-entity (if John Doe is private) OR needs PII-check; instruction-following: n/a

5) Raw: "Assistant: I cannot help with tax advice; you should consult an accountant."
   Labels: instruction-following: refuses (policy-compliant); content-quality: concise

Ambiguous boundaries (discussion notes):
- Partial vs hallucination: if model attempts to answer with incorrect facts -> label as factual-error (hallucination). If model skips steps or omits required pieces but the provided content is factually correct -> partial.
- Refusal vs safe content: refusal that cites a policy (eg. cannot provide medical diagnosis) should be labeled 'refuses' + tag for 'policy-compliant'. If assistant provides a high-level safe summary, label 'ok' + 'safe'.

Annotation guidelines (short):
- Always read full conversation context (last 3 turns) before labeling.
- Prefer conservative labeling when unsure: tag for review rather than assign definitive label. Use 'needs-review' (mapped in the tooling).
- For multi-label cases, list all applicable labels separated by semicolon; primary label first.

Quality control checks (post-annotation):
- Automated rules to catch obvious mismatches:
  * If 'hallucination' assigned but answer matches a reliable KB (we have small local index) -> flag for human review
  * If PII placeholder used but original had only partial name (first name) -> flag for possible over-redaction
- Sampling plan: weekly random sample of 200 annotated items, run with Asha+Ryan review, target disagreement < 5% on primary label for acceptance

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need canonical list of 'sensitive entities' (orgs vs people) — ask Security for list and KMS requirements for replacements (ticket JIRA-DATA-4328).
- Decide whether to permanently remove low-quality turns or keep them with label 'low-quality' (impact on model learning).
- Define final taxonomy and map to training labels (one-hot vs multi-label).
- Prepare 30 canonical samples with edge-case coverage (I'll draft 15; Asha to add 15).

Notes to self / shortcuts:
- When writing final guidelines, include a 1-page cheat-sheet for raters with 8-10 canonical examples.
- Add quick regex snippets in a follow-up doc for PII detection (SSN, CC, emails, phone).
- Add an internal confluence link to final taxonomy once merged: CONFLUENCE-DataLabeling-Edgecases (placeholder).

Sign-off checklist for turning into a 'final' doc:
- [ ] Resolve open questions above
- [ ] Sync with Security and Legal on PII handling
- [ ] Produce sample set (30 examples) and seed the annotation queue
- [ ] Run first week of sampling and adjust heuristics

End of scratchpad.

(Handy refs: CONFLUENCE-DataLabeling-Overview; JIRA-DATA-4321 for annotation infra; PR #87 for the cleanup scripts.)
